title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
keyIdea: Dummy before head; bef = node before the current group. Check k nodes exist (kthNode); if not, stop. Reverse in place by moving the node after start to the group front k − 1 times. Then bef = start (the old first node is now last).

approaches.name: Recursion with getLength
approaches.idea: If at least k nodes remain, reverse the first k, recurse on the rest and attach it to the old head.
approaches.why: getLength walks the whole remaining list in every call; one call per group on the stack. Counting only k nodes ahead would make it O(n).

approaches.name: Iterative with a dummy node
approaches.idea: kthNode walks k steps from bef. Full group → start = bef->next, curr = start->next; k − 1 times: start->next = curr->next, curr->next = bef->next, bef->next = curr, curr = start->next. Then bef = start.
approaches.why: Each node is visited a constant number of times; only a few pointers.

quiz.q: Why check that k nodes exist before reversing?
options: A last group with fewer than k nodes must stay in its original order

quiz.q: What do the three lines in the inner loop do?
options: Take curr out, point it at the group front, make it the new front

quiz.q: Why bef = start after a group?
options: start was the group's first node and is now its last, so it sits right before the next group

quiz.q: Why is the commented recursive version slower than O(n)?
options: getLength walks the entire remaining list in every call
